summary.text: Nicolaus Copernicus was a Renaissance polymath who formulated a model of the universe that placed the Sun, rather than Earth, at its center.
His book On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres, published just before his death in 1543, triggered the Copernican Revolution and contributed to the Scientific Revolution.
A similar heliocentric model was developed eighteen centuries earlier by Aristarchus of Samos, but Copernicus likely arrived at his own independently.

facts.label: Main book
facts.value: De revolutionibus orbium coelestium, published in 1543

facts.label: Economics
facts.value: Derived a quantity theory of money in 1517

facts.label: Education
facts.value: Obtained a doctorate in canon law

items.prompt: A stargazer in 1550 reads Copernicus and redraws her chart of the universe. What does she put at the middle?

options.label: The Earth
The Sun
The Moon
Jupiter

items.explain: Copernicus formulated a model of the universe that placed the Sun rather than Earth at its center.

items.prompt: A classmate says Copernicus must have copied his model from an ancient Greek astronomer. What do historians say?

options.label: He read the Greek work and credited its author
He copied it, since the models were identical
A similar model was lost and never studied
A similar model existed, but he likely reached his independently

items.explain: Aristarchus of Samos developed a similar heliocentric model eighteen centuries earlier, but Copernicus likely arrived at his model independently.

items.prompt: Copernicus also worked outside astronomy. What economic idea is credited to him?

options.label: A quantity theory of money, derived in 1517
A system of paper money backed by copper
A rule for setting interest on merchant loans
A tax on cities that traded along the Vistula

items.explain: In 1517 he derived a quantity theory of money, and in 1519 he formulated a principle later called Gresham's law.

items.prompt: Who was Lucas Watzenrode the Younger to Copernicus?

options.label: His father, a merchant who traded copper
His teacher at the University of Kraków
His rival, who opposed his career in the Church
His maternal uncle and patron, who became Bishop of Warmia

items.explain: Lucas Watzenrode the Younger was the astronomer's maternal uncle and patron, and he was elected Bishop of Warmia in 1489.

items.prompt: Copernicus's major book appeared just before his death. What was its effect?

options.label: It ended the Scientific Revolution
It was an early work of the Scientific Revolution only in name
It proved that Aristarchus had been wrong
It triggered the Copernican Revolution

items.explain: The book was a major event in the history of science, triggering the Copernican Revolution and contributing to the Scientific Revolution.

items.prompt: A friend says Copernicus was only an astronomer. What best corrects that?

options.label: He was mainly a soldier who watched the sky at night
He was also a physician, diplomat, governor and economist
He was a merchant like his father with a hobby
He was a priest with no scientific training

items.explain: He was a polymath: a mathematician, astronomer, physician, classics scholar, translator, governor, diplomat and economist.
